# Stage P-bis — Miliarium pool seeding transaction ledger

Chain 11155111. Broadcaster `0xA851478dbee97375E784e9b98c0D7D599662bF85`, the deployer EOA rather than the multisig per PB-D46, because initialization is permissionless and its caller becomes the pool first BPT holder. On Sepolia those are the same address per PB-D23 (iv).

The complete per-transaction ledger for the `SeedMiliariumPoolsSepolia` run that capitalised all 26 Miliarium Aureum pools. Generated from `broadcast/SeedMiliariumPoolsSepolia.s.sol/11155111/run-latest.json` rather than transcribed, and regenerating it must reproduce this file byte for byte. `broadcast/` is gitignored, so this is the committed record of what that artifact holds. Narrative, aggregates and the on-chain TVL verification are in `docs/STAGE_P_BIS_SEPOLIA_DEPLOYMENT_RECORD.md` section 13.

The arguments column records the seeding amounts as actually sent, so the authored allocation table in `script/config/MiliariumSeedAllocations.sol` can be checked against the chain by a later reader with no RPC access. That table is authored rather than derived, so this ledger is the only external evidence of what it produced.

## GENERATION 1 — ABANDONED

Abandoned with the whole generation-1 contract set at PB3.13 per PB-D70 (i). These 26 pools hold real seeded capital on chain and are the only abandoned generation that does, generation 2 having died at its wiring before any pool was seeded. The table below is unchanged executed history and does NOT describe live protocol state. One correction to the byte-for-byte regeneration claim above: `broadcast/SeedMiliariumPoolsSepolia.s.sol/11155111/run-latest.json` now holds the GENERATION 3 run, so these rows can no longer be regenerated from that artifact and are checkable only against the chain.

Transactions 389, receipts 389, every one successful. Nonces 301 to 689, contiguous. Blocks 11405061 to 11405532. Total gas 33,643,685. Breakdown: approve 177, mint 127, deposit 59, initialize 26.

## GENERATION 3 — LIVE

The generation-3 seeding, executed 2026-08-16, capitalising all 26 Miliarium Aureum pools against the generation-3 Vault and Router. 330 transactions against generation 1's 389, and the 59-transaction difference is documented idempotency rather than a shortfall: `_approve` skips its ERC-20 leg to Permit2 whenever the existing allowance suffices, and the 87 stubs are reused unchanged per PB-D70 (i), so generation 1's `type(uint256).max` approvals to canonical Permit2 still stand. The Permit2-to-Router leg cannot skip, the Router having moved, and all 59 of those fire. Both halves were read on chain before the broadcast: the ERC-20 allowance to Permit2 returns `type(uint256).max`, the Permit2 allowance to generation 1's Router still returns `type(uint160).max`, and the same read against generation 3's Router returns zero. 389 is therefore the count for a FIRST seeding and 330 the count for a refresh; a future generation would see 330 again. Gas is 29,430,430 against generation 1's 33,643,685, and the 4,213,255 difference has two causes rather than one: the 59 absent approvals, and every mint landing on a balance slot already warm from generation 1, which is why nonce 1118's mint cost 50,997 where its generation-1 twin at nonce 301 cost 68,097. der Bodensee is NOT seeded here; `isPoolInitialized` returns false for it and `tvl` reverts `PoolNotInitialized`, its dust initialization and first distribute being PB3.9 per PB-D68 (xi).

Transactions 330, receipts 330, every one successful. Nonces 1118 to 1447, contiguous. Blocks 11503647 to 11504040. Total gas 29,430,430. Breakdown: mint 127, approve 118, deposit 59, initialize 26.
